title: How many whole units does three halves contain?
description: Three halves is written as three halves added together. The board groups two halves into one whole unit and finds one half left over. Keeko doubts the answer by reading the top number as the number of whole units.
teaching_notes: One idea: a fraction greater than one holds as many whole units as there are full groups of the bottom number in the top number. Watch for students who take the top number as the count of whole units.

source: How many whole units does 3/2 contain?
video_script.why: A learner finds the whole units inside a fraction greater than one by grouping its halves.
video_script.substitution: the book's own fraction three halves
video_script.anchor: three half-unit bars on a number line from 0 to 2
video_script.wrong_answer: three halves has three whole units, because the top number is three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko reads the top number as the number of whole units, though each unit needs two halves.
video_script.payoff_line: Three halves contains one whole unit

final_answer.spoken: three halves contains one whole unit, with one half left over

maths_rules: 3/2 means 3 parts, each 1/2 of a unit
video_script.design: Three half-unit bars laid on the number line from zero. Two halves join into one whole bar and one half stays alone.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a number line from 0 to 2 with each unit cut into two parts; the black line of 3/2 from 0

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.line: the number line appears with each unit cut into two equal parts
marks.black: the black line of three halves is drawn from zero and passes the mark one

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book, and it uses a number line.
<bookmark mark='line'/>Each unit on this number line is cut into two equal parts.
<bookmark mark='black'/>The black line is three halves long and passes the mark one.
How many whole units does three halves contain?

beats.on_screen: the number line and the black line stay; the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: the fraction 3/2 shown as three half bars; a whole unit bar beside them

marks.means: three half bars of equal size line up from zero
marks.whole: a whole unit bar is shown beside them, as long as two half bars

narration: <bookmark mark='means'/>Three halves means three parts, and each part is one half of a unit.
<bookmark mark='whole'/>A whole unit is the same length as two of those halves.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the fraction that we have to look at is three halves.

beats.on_screen: To find: how many whole units 3/2 contains
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how many whole units this fraction contains.

marks.split: three halves is written as three halves added together

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step one, write three halves as three halves added together. That is one half plus one half plus one half.

marks.join: the first two half bars join and become one whole unit bar

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step two, two halves make one whole. The first two halves join to make one whole unit.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: one half is left over

marks.left: the third half bar stays alone, after the whole unit

narration: <bookmark mark='left'/>Step three, the third half cannot make another whole unit by itself. One half is left over.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 halves + 1 half = 3 halves, the same as 3/2

marks.check: the whole unit and the left over half are put back together as three halves

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>To check, put the pieces back. Two halves and one half make three halves again.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Three halves contains one whole unit.
It also has one more half left over after that whole unit.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the number line
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a bubble says 3/2 has 3 whole units because the top number is 3; the three halves are grouped and only one whole forms; the bubble is struck out

marks.doubt: the bubble with the wrong idea appears
marks.group: the three half bars are grouped in twos and only one whole forms
marks.fix: the bubble is struck out and the top number is marked as a count of halves

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks three halves has three whole units, because the top number is three.
<bookmark mark='group'/>Group the halves in twos. Only one group of two forms, with one half left.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The top number counts the halves, not the whole units.
